name: Executive Command Center
description: Portfolio and project health, commitments, decision requests and training launchpad
help: Always separate team-level progress from integrated project delivery, financial exposure and measurable customer outcomes.

name: Data Integrity & Verification
description: Internal value consistency, financial controls, date checks and management review flags
help: Internal checks identify invalid or inconsistent sample records. Only responsible real-system owners can verify source evidence and approvals.

name: Demand & Portfolio Kanban
description: Ideas, strategic fit, triage and investment decisions
help: A request is not automatically an approved project. Capture the customer problem, expected value, options, sponsor and portfolio decision.

name: Business Case & Benefits
description: Outcome hypothesis, baseline, measurable target and benefit ownership
help: Quantify current state, target, operational benefits, cost, evidence and benefit owner. Capacity freed is not automatically cash saved.

name: Charter & Scope
description: Charter, project boundaries, acceptance, exclusions and authorization
help: A sponsor approves the project mandate and authorized constraints. A date proposed by the business is not automatically a validated baseline.

name: Stakeholders & RACI
description: Influence, authority, engagement, role boundaries and accountable decisions
help: RACI clarifies responsibility; decision rights must name the person who can actually authorize funding, risk or release.

name: RACI Matrix
description: Named responsibilities for project and program activities
help: Assign one accountable person and at least one responsible person per activity. List people to consult before the decision and people to inform afterward.

name: Integrated Roadmap
description: Milestones, baseline versus forecast, owners and dependencies
help: Do not copy sprint tasks into the integrated plan. Manage milestone commitments, external dependencies and release forecasts.

name: Agile Epics & Features
description: Epics, features, stories, acceptance criteria and sprint mapping
help: PO owns backlog ordering and clarification. Scrum team owns implementation and quality. PM views cross-team commitments.

name: Sprint & PI Objectives
description: Iteration outcomes, PI objectives, confidence and integrated demos
help: Daily Scrum belongs to Developers; the Scrum Master ensures Scrum effectiveness. PM does not use it for status collection.

name: Cross-Team Dependencies
description: Producer/consumer contracts, handoffs, integration deadlines and escalation
help: Track exact deliverable, producing team, consuming team, needed-by date, impact, owner and evidence.

name: Resources & Capacity
description: People, allocation, support reserve, available skill capacity
help: Availability is not usable delivery capacity. Account for production support, enterprise Okta work, leave and skill bottlenecks.

name: Budget & Forecast
description: Budget, actuals, ETC, EAC, variance, contingency and commitments
help: EAC = actuals + estimate to complete. A project can be under budget today yet have a projected overrun.

name: RAID Register
description: Risks, assumptions, issues and dependencies with mitigation ownership
help: Risk: may happen. Issue: already happened. Document trigger, consequence, owner, action, due date and escalation.

name: Change Control
description: Scope, schedule and funding changes with impact assessment and approval
help: PO can reprioritize within delegated scope; material changes to approved baseline require authorized decisions.

name: Decision & Escalation Log
description: Decision request, tradeoff, authority, due date and evidence
help: PM coordinates decisions, but does not automatically own all approvals. Escalate outside authority with recommendation.

name: Quality & Test Management
description: SIT, E2E, UAT, defects, nonfunctional controls and evidence
help: QA Lead owns test execution and quality evidence; PM owns integrated readiness and disposition of blocked milestones.

name: Release Readiness
description: Go/no-go controls, deployment, customer exposure and rollback
help: Distinguish deploying software from exposing a capability to customers. Confirm authority, operational controls and business recovery.

name: Hypercare & Operations
description: Support readiness, incidents, stability and operational handover
help: Code rollback may not undo policy transactions. Plan data reconciliation, support ownership and hypercare exit thresholds.

name: Vendors & Contracts
description: Contracts, obligations, vendor SLAs and delivery commitments
help: Vendor milestones need named owners, acceptance evidence, escalation paths and cost consequences.

name: Security & Insurance Controls
description: Privacy, access, jurisdiction, audit, underwriting and accessibility
help: For Add/Replace Vehicle, confirm eligibility, policy effective dates, rating, consent, audit trail and exceptions with control owners.

name: Status & Governance
description: RAG status, steering decisions, evidence and communications
help: Green sprints can coexist with a Red project. Report integrated forecast, confidence, financials, top blockers and decisions.

name: Recovery & Scenarios
description: Recovery assessment, decision options and controlled rebaselining
help: Do not change a Red project to Green by changing labels. Diagnose, stabilize, compare options, approve new baseline and track evidence.

name: Program Coordination
description: Related projects, program outcomes, shared dependencies, benefit realization
help: A program is related initiatives managed together for benefits. Not every collection of teams constitutes a program.

name: SAFe & Lean Portfolio
description: Portfolio Kanban, value streams, ART, PI planning, WSJF and guardrails
help: SAFe concepts do not replace actual governance. Operational and development value streams are distinct; funding authority remains explicit.

name: Value Stream Mapping
description: Flow stages, wait time, bottlenecks, handoffs, leading and lagging measures
help: Map work from customer need to actual value. Distinguish active working time and queue time; measure improvements.

name: Organizational Change
description: Stakeholder adoption, communication, training, resistance and change outcomes
help: Transformation is not only new ceremonies. Track whether business roles adopt the changed operating model.

name: Project Closure
description: Acceptance, financial closure, lessons learned and benefits ownership
help: Separate project closure from ongoing product ownership and long-term benefits measurement.

name: Learning Academy
description: Guided instruction, practice questions, scenarios and answer feedback
help: Use practice mode to make accountable decisions instead of memorizing definitions.

name: Full Reference Library
description: Complete brand-neutral training guide, design assumptions and help glossary
help: Reference guide contains an additional FNOL case; primary interactive workspace stays Add/Replace Vehicle.
